title: Cross-Sectional Relative Strength
market_behavior: Assets that recently led peers may continue leading when capital rotates gradually across sectors, styles, countries, or asset classes.
forced_actor: Model portfolios, performance-chasing allocators, mandate-bound managers, and funds gradually changing exposure.
why_edge_might_exist: Relative leadership may persist when allocators adjust slowly and when investor attention follows recent winners.
why_large_capital_may_ignore_it: Broad momentum is well studied and crowded; smaller or fragmented universes may have lower capacity and higher turnover costs.
capacity_hypothesis: Capacity is likely high for broad ETFs but the edge may be low; more interesting variants may require narrower, less-liquid universes.
observable_predictions: A prespecified relative-strength rotation should improve risk-adjusted performance versus a static benchmark.
The result should survive walk-forward validation and neighboring-universe checks.
falsification_tests: Reject if walk-forward out-of-sample windows fail.
Reject if performance depends on one tuned lookback or top-N choice.
Weaken if turnover costs erase the advantage.
references: Practitioner literature on ETF relative-strength rotation
